reviews.title: Perfect sturdy desk

reviews.author: Lars

reviews.title: High Quality Walking Pad Desk
reviews.body: I dont write many reviews, but I searched the internet high and low for the best standing desk option at a good price & I picked a winner! I was hoping for black, but wanted the most practical over color. This one is perfectly functional for my needs & I got it in the wish-list black as a bonus. You can set this to 4 different heights. I only plan to use this over my walking pad & set at the tallest height is the ideal spot for me at 5'6". I knew when I saw this large desk packed into a small, very compact box that there was going to be in a lot of pieces. When I saw just how many pieces and bolts, I was a little overwhelmed & almost decided to leave it for my husband to assemble. He wasnt home and I was ready to use it, so reluctantly I gave it go. It wasnt that bad! The instructions suggest 2 people for assembly, but honestly its not needed & you'd just in each other's way. I put it together, by myself, in about 45 minutes. It's a solid, good quality piece. The locking casters make it a sturdy work surface. If you're looking for a simple but sturdy desk so that you can work while getting in steps, I dont think you'll be disappointed with this one
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 11, 2025
reviews.author: Shannon Silcox

reviews.title: The functionality is okay, but the height is a major issue
reviews.body: The functionality is okay, but the height is a major issue. I bought this because other reviews mentioned it was a decent size, so I want to be really clear for anyone around my height or taller.I’m 5'4", and even with the desk fully extended to its highest setting, it’s still not tall enough for working while walking. I have a walking pad set to a 6% incline, and even with that in mind, the desk height just doesn’t work.For reference:When I’m standing on the floor, the top of the desk comes to under my chest/mid-rib area.When I’m on my walking pad, it only reaches slightly above my belly button, which is way too low to type on comfortably.I will now have to buy or add something underneath my laptop to raise it several more inches. If you’re taller than me, this desk likely won’t work for you without modifications.Stability:It’s decent. Not super sturdy, but not wobbly enough to be a deal-breaker—pretty much what you expect for a Black Friday deal.Assembly:This took me about 4.5 hours total to build by myself. I started at 2:45 PM and wasn’t fully done until around 8:30 PM, although I did have to step away multiple times for my kids. If you don’t have several hours to dedicate, or if you’re not someone who likes long assembly projects, just be aware of the time commitment. The ease of use I would say was the hardest part of this purchase by having to put it all together but u enjoy puzzles.And if you have pets—keep them away while unpacking. My dog immediately ran over and peed on the parts and the instructions, which added extra cleaning time and definitely slowed everything down. But even with all the interruptions, I managed to get it done in one day.Overall, it’s fine for the price, but the height limitations are a big drawback. If you’re around my height or taller and plan to use it with a walking pad, you’ll probably need to buy risers or a laptop stand to make it workable.I do have to say I like how it looks overall, except that there was chipping on the wood desk panels right from the box.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 3, 2025
reviews.author: Jessica Marshall

reviews.title: Unsturdy, wiggly, unstable… Not usable
reviews.body: Probably one of the worst standing desks. Super wiggly, in fact, part of the wheels just don’t touch the floor. It’s also super unstable and unusable with the walking pad. Size is okay, height is okay, but definitely not worth getting it; for the same amount ($60-70) you could get a higher quality standing desk, and even for the discounted price of $50, just pay the extra dollars for something better.It’s also marketed as usable with a treadmill but wow, the shakiness of the table is not real…
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 13, 2025
